solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Smith's girl deviously dumping lecturer's wrong? Not her

indicators.note: going deviously means taking a twisted route, so the letters of the first words are rearranged
dumping means throwing out, so the letter for the lecturer is discarded from the pool

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lecturer, as on a learner's plate

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's daughter is accused of misleading a lecturer, though she is said to be blameless.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle SMITHSGIRL less L. The definition plays on the idiom Mr Right: the ideal partner is never wrong, so the perfect woman is the one who is 'not wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the ideal partner a woman or man hopes to marry, playfully described as someone who is never in error.

clue.text: Conceptualise one meeting involving leader of executives

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the first pieces wrap around the letter from executives

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone at a business meeting with the head of the executives is asked to come up with ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to form an idea or picture something in the mind is to conceive or imagine it.

clue.text: Could be Sir Philip Denis out with Yorkshire opener

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the name are rearranged
the opener of a word is its first letter, with a nod to an opening batsman

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a batsman called Denis has been dismissed alongside the Yorkshire opening bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' and 'opener' suggest cricket, but 'out' rearranges DENIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Sir Philip Sidney was the Elizabethan poet and courtier, so the first name is what 'Sir Philip' could be completed with.

clue.text: Poor do. Is it they who are responsible?

definitions.note: the plural fools who are to blame for a poor show

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a disappointing party, someone asks whether the blame lies with a particular group.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic hint: after a poor do, fools are the people to blame, hence the question mark.

clue.text: The Yard's tipsy soak

indicators.note: tipsy means unsteady with drink, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk police officer from Scotland Yard, a soak, is the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a noun for a drunkard; it is the verb. The Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to drench something with water or make it take up moisture.

clue.text: Palace casually giving foreign money audience

parts.note: a buck is an American dollar, foreign money to a British solver
a house is a theatre audience, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A palace is paid in foreign currency to grant a royal audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name: Buckingham Palace, the monarch's London residence, is jokingly shortened this way.

clue.text: Worn-out tutor's painting

parts.note: something worn-out is old
a master is a teacher in a school

explanation.surface: An exhausted teacher's picture is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a great European artist's work from before about 1800, or that artist, is known by this term.

clue.text: Thwarted Derek turning up, having cropped scarf on top

indicators.note: in a down entry, on top means placed above, so this piece comes first
cropped means cut short, so the last letter of the scarf word goes

parts.note: a snood is a hood-like scarf

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: Derek arrives wearing a cut-down scarf and finds his plans blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cropped' trims SNOOD to SNOO; 'turning up' turns DEREK to KERED, placed below.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker idiom: a player left with no direct shot is blocked, so the word means frustrated or obstructed.

clue.text: Fabric problem's nothing, on independent reflection

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the second piece follows the first
a reflection is a mirror image, so the word for a problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

indicators.note: independent here means separately mirrored too, so the word for nothing is also read backwards on its own

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone thinking things over alone decides their problem is nothing after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'independent reflection' means each piece is turned on its own: SUM becomes MUS, NIL becomes LIN, not the pair turned as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fine, loosely woven cotton cloth used for dresses and in the kitchen.

clue.text: His Excellency says more about victory blows

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for saying more goes round the victory

parts.note: adds means says further
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: An ambassador adds a few words about a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: winds against one's direction of travel are blows of air hampering progress.

clue.text: Seaman accepts novel with love and with open arms

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the sailor's letters hold the novel

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A sailor warmly embraces a book and a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: standing with hands on hips and elbows turned outward is a posture with the arms spread open.

clue.text: Vehicle giving way to another

parts.note: a street is a way or road
another vehicle, carrying on from the definition: a car

explanation.surface: A road user yields to a second vehicle at a junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' borrows its noun from the definition: another vehicle, a CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the American word for a tram, a public transport car running on rails in the road.

clue.text: Mix us some dessert

indicators.note: to mix is to stir together, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to whisk up a pudding for the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light, airy pudding made with whipped cream or egg white, often chocolate.

clue.text: Seasoning the bill — pound on slate, possibly

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in pick up the tab
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill for seasoning, a pound chalked up on the slate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on slate' suggests credit at a pub, with 'slate' the tab owed; here 'possibly' works on the word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ordinary salt for the dinner table is the commonest seasoning.

clue.text: Not where grub alone is served

definitions.text: Not where grub alone is served

indicators.note: served up as a dish, the letters are prepared afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: A place that is not just for food but for drinks too.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a pub room where drink, not food alone, is served.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the more comfortable room of a British pub, where drinks are the main business rather than meals only.

clue.text: Graph showing frequency of the chap's girl mounting

parts.note: his means belonging to the chap

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing, so the name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Margot is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man's girlfriend climbing higher is charted on a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a bar chart whose bar areas represent how often values fall within each range.

clue.text: Poultry farmer who took part in court action?

definitions.text: who took part in court action?
definitions.meaning: Tim ..., the British tennis player who played on the courts

explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: a chicken keeper, and the surname of Tim Henman, Britain's leading tennis player of the 1990s and 2000s.

clue.text: The Mendips' edge

indicators.note: the possessive apostrophe says the letters belong to the words, held inside them

explanation.surface: The rim of the Mendip Hills is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips are a range of hills in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a border or rim, especially the folded edge of cloth.

clue.text: Some banana bread

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie within the word

explanation.surface: A slice of banana bread is offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banana bread' looks like one phrase; 'bread' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a leavened flatbread from South Asia baked in a tandoor oven.

clue.text: Poison yielding awful reaction. It's not right

indicators.note: awful means terrible or mangled, so the word's letters are rearranged
not means without, so the letter for right is excluded

explanation.surface: Someone suffers a terrible response to a poison and something is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: REACTION without R gives EACTION, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: monkshood, a plant whose roots contain a deadly toxin.

clue.text: Harsh wind before end of cruise

indicators.note: before means coming earlier, so the wind word precedes the letter

parts.note: Auster is the south wind, from Latin

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A rough wind blows up just as a sea voyage ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: severe, stern or plain to the point of hardship.

clue.text: See 17
Rarely mixing, also involved with CIA internally

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the agency's letters go within
involved means tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy who seldom socialises gets caught up with the CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: not sociable, avoiding company, so seldom mixing with others.

clue.text: Aunt attacked in the French crescent?

definitions.note: a noun standing for its adjective, crescent-shaped

indicators.note: in means inside, so the scrambled relative goes within the article

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: attacked means set upon, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A relative assaulted in a French street called a crescent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crescent' is used as an adjective (crescent moon), hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: shaped like a new moon, from Latin luna.

clue.text: Stevedore seen in cutter?

definitions.meaning: a dock worker who loads ships
one who docks, that is cuts short, as a dog's tail is docked

explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: a worker at the port, and whimsically a person who docks or trims.

clue.text: Inattentive when PM rises

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: in a down entry, rises means goes upward, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister dozes off while getting up to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: not alert or paying attention, as if sleeping.

clue.text: Monkey showing energy on tree-top

parts.note: verve means energy or vigour

indicators.note: in a down entry, the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monkey shows great vigour atop a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an African monkey with a black face and greenish-grey coat.

clue.text: Persian prophet is cross on a very hot day

parts.note: a zo is a cross between a yak and a cow
a roaster is informally a scorching day

explanation.surface: A Persian prophet is irritable on a sweltering day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry'; it is the hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the founder of the ancient Iranian religion is known by this Greek form of his name.

clue.text: Conveyance that will distract at the Gabba

definitions.meaning: a vehicle that moves over snow on runners

definitions.text: that will distract at the Gabba
definitions.meaning: in cricket, to taunt a batsman to break concentration; the Gabba is a cricket ground in Brisbane

explanation.definitionFit: Double sense: a sled for travel on snow, and the Australian cricketing verb for verbally needling a batsman.

clue.text: One trims half of street in time off work

parts.note: a sickle is a tool for cutting grass

indicators.note: half of means the first half of the word is taken

parts.note: an avenue is a street

explanation.surface: A gardener trims half a street during a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: absence from work allowed because of illness.

clue.text: We could have fifty animals with these in

indicators.note: in means inside, so the Roman fifty goes within the speakers' word

parts.note: the speakers are lamas, Tibetan Buddhist monks
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Monks musing that they might keep fifty beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We' is spoken by Tibetan monks, LAMAS; put L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: South American pack animals related to the camel.

clue.text: Enlightening guide to landing in narrow semi round back

indicators.note: back means returning, so the whole construction is read backwards
round means surrounding, so the half word goes about the narrowing word

parts.note: semi means half
to taper is to narrow

explanation.surface: A clearly lit approach to an airfield in a thin semi-detached house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' looks like a British semi-detached house, but it means half. 'back' turns the whole assembly, giving HTAPERALF reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a line of lights marking a runway so that aircraft can land at night.
